compute.cost_note: Pure stdlib regex and counting heuristics; no model, network, or GPU.

do_not_use_when: You need a definitive document-type classification, calibrated probability, authorship verdict, or AI/human judgment; these scores are uncalibrated compatibility heuristics.
You need to distinguish document types collapsed within one family, such as legal briefs from grant proposals.

inputs.target: Prose text plus an optional canonical, family, or deprecated register hint; register_match also accepts baseline register declarations.

artifacts: In-memory classify_register and register_match dictionaries carrying the register_families/v2 taxonomy marker.

purpose: Classify prose into one of eight scorer-backed register families and compare that family with canonical manifest register declarations so voice-distance reports expose register mismatch instead of silently treating every baseline as comparable.
use_when: You need a lightweight, stdlib-only register-family compatibility check before interpreting voice distance.
You need canonical voiceprint manifest registers or deprecated classifier spellings resolved into the versioned register_families/v2 vocabulary.
